partner_results_applied.result: translation-uniform half-Riesz bound for every invertible indefinite binary quadratic: sup_t E|t-R|^-1/2 <=16 sqrt(2)|det S|^-1/4
physical indefinite-pair logarithmic transducer: residual H sqrt(rho) small-ball implies density <=4 sqrt(2H)(D kappa)^-1/4

new_result.statement: For every symmetric physical 3x3 B with sigma_min(B)>=s>0 and every independent cap-one triple, arbitrary affine perturbations of X^T B X have density sup <= C3/s, C3=16 sqrt(2)(1601/512)^(1/8)=26.093068347867227. The same bound holds for an ambient quadratic form after conditioning outside any such original-coordinate principal triple.
new_result.proof_mechanism: Diagonal/off-diagonal dichotomy. A large physical diagonal is handled by one square pivot plus either the partner indefinite binary half-Riesz theorem or an elementary definite ellipsoid bound. If all diagonals are small, row norm forces a quantitatively indefinite physical pair; pair completion leaves a scalar square and the partner logarithmic transducer applies. Optimizing the split gives c^2=512/1601.
new_result.time_integral: Downstream of the density theorem, |phi|^2=phi_(q-q') and Plancherel give int |phi|^2 <=2 pi C3/s without breaking sum/difference dependence.
new_result.target_example: B0=[[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,0]] has spectrum {2,-1,-1}; the sharper branch constant is 8.

unresolved_implication: The bare three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis does not force a uniformly conditioned physical principal triple. An aggregate-before-inversion product-coordinate compiler is still needed to route every target matrix into this branch or existing ridge/diffuse/grouped-bank/mixed-hub branches.
